subject: VoltEdge private offer: upfront payment request, discount & rev-share exception
messages:
From: Erin Walsh <erin@voltedge.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer - request: 30% discount + upfront payment schedule + rev-share update

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at VoltEdge is excited about Redwood's latency profile and the dedicated capacity options. Procurement asked me to submit the formal request for the private offer so we can move to an internal approval. High level ask: a 36-month commitment with a 30% list discount and a preference to pay 50% upfront followed by annual invoices. Also asking for a rev-share adjustment from the standard 60/40 to 70/30 in VoltEdge's favor for the first 12 months to offset integration costs.

We understand those are outside standard marketplace terms, so I attached our procurement form and a short summary of the business case. Can you escalate for executive approval? We are ready to sign quickly if the commercial levers align.

Attachments: VoltEdge_Procurement_Form.pdf, VoltEdge_Terms_Summary.xlsx

Thanks,
Erin Walsh
Head of Partnerships
VoltEdge

Subject: Fwd: Private offer - request: 30% discount + upfront payment schedule + rev-share update

Team — forwarding VoltEdge's formal ask. Key deviators: 30% list discount, 50% upfront payment, and an initial 70/30 rev-share in their favor for 12 months.

Karthik: can you run the margin/commission impact and advise recommended exceptions? If deal desk cannot approve the discount/rev-share, please draft alternative structuring (e.g., smaller discount + upfront credit, capped rev-share for 6 months, or performance-based credit tied to usage).

Marissa: breaking threshold is >25% discount and any rev-share >65/35 requires senior sales approval per policy — tagging you for exec guidance.

Laura: legal, please flag any contract obligations or clause language we should require for the rev-share carve (audit rights, data residency, termination triggers).

I will respond to Erin with a timeline once we have internal alignment.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 14:20:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer - request: 30% discount + upfront payment schedule + rev-share update

Quick analysis from Deal Desk:

- Baseline: Standard private-offer commission / rev-share splits in marketplace listings are 60/40 (customer/redwood). Moving to 70/30 in customer's favor for 12 months reduces platform revenue materially and sets a precedent.
- Discount: 30% off list for a 36-month term is outside the delegated approval (we can do up to 20% by desk). Incremental discount beyond 20% will materially extend payback on our committed capacity.
- Upfront: A 50% upfront payment helps cash flow, but net terms request (they asked annual after that) impacts ARR recognition and might trigger finance review.

Recommended options to present to the customer (in order of preference):
1) Approve a one-time upfront invoice credit equal to 20% of first-year ARR if they pay 50% upfront and commit to 36 months; keep rev-share at 60/40 but add a 6-month temporary uplift to 65/35 if usage exceeds the forecasted thresholds (metric-based ramp).
2) If an exec-level concession is necessary, escalate for approval of up to 25% discount and a 65/35 rev-share for 3 months only, with strict audit rights and clawback if usage/ARR thresholds are not met.
3) Deny 30% list discount and 70/30 rev-share; offer an alternate commercial construct: 25% discount + 50% upfront + marketing co-fund in lieu of higher rev-share.

I can prepare the spreadsheet with modeled IRR/ARR impacts and commission adjustments; need Marissa or finance to sign off on any >20% discount or rev-share deviation >65/35.

Karthik
Deal Desk Lead
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>; Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Oct 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer - request: 30% discount + upfront payment schedule + rev-share update

Thanks Karthik for the options. High level decision from sales leadership: we will not approve a standing 70/30 rev-share. However, I will authorize the following exec exception, contingent on finance and legal signoff:

- Approve a one-time invoice credit equal to 30% of the first invoice (applied as an upfront commercial concession) if VoltEdge pays 50% upfront on signing and commits to 36 months.
- Rev-share: cap temporary uplift to 65/35 in VoltEdge's favor for the first 3 months only, and then revert to standard 60/40 thereafter. The uplift must be tied to usage thresholds (we will set three revenue/usage gates in the private offer).
- Require clawback clause: if VoltEdge terminates early or usage falls below 60% of forecast in months 1-3, clawback the uplifted portion.

Laura: please draft the contract language for the clawback, audit rights, and the private offer terms. Finance: need confirmation that a 30% upfront invoice credit is acceptable for revenue recognition and billing flow.

Sean — if VoltEdge accepts these constraints, you may proceed to send the private offer draft with the marketplace link and request the PO/confirmation. If they push back on rev-share >65/35, we hold firm.

Marissa Cole
VP, Sales, Americas
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin@voltedge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Oct 2025 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer - request: 30% discount + upfront payment schedule + rev-share update

Erin — thanks for the patience while we escalated internally. Condensed update and next steps below.

What we can approve (executive exception):
- A one-time commercial concession equal to 30% applied as an upfront invoice credit on the first invoice if VoltEdge pays 50% of the contract value at signing and commits to a 36-month private offer.
- Temporary rev-share uplift to 65/35 in VoltEdge's favor for months 1-3 only; after month 3 the rev-share will revert to the standard 60/40. The 65/35 uplift is conditional on the customer hitting the agreed usage gates.
- Required contract clauses: audit rights, clawback for early termination or under-usage, and specific termination triggers. Laura and finance are drafting the exact language.

What we cannot approve: a standing 70/30 rev-share for 12 months and an unconditional 30% list discount without conditions.

Next steps:
1) I'll send the private offer draft via the AWS private offer flow (link attached) with the above terms and the invoice credit reflected as a billing concession.
2) Please confirm you can do 50% upfront at signing and provide a PO referencing DEAL-8721-VE.
3) Once we receive PO and upfront payment, legal/finance will finalize the private offer and we will publish the marketplace listing.

Attachments: private-offer-draft-link.txt (contains the AWS private-offer draft link)
